mainTopic: What the inner goat of יום כיפור atones for, and how רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון learn it
overview: The גמרא keeps asking which sins the inner goat of יום כיפור could atone for. It first shows that some cases of גילוי עריות and שפיכות דמים are not covered by death, by a קרבן, or by גלות. Examples are a sin done on purpose with no warning, or by accident without ever finding out. Then it quotes the ברייתא: רבי יהודה learns from 'מִטֻּמְאוֹת' that the goat covers only טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, the one טומאה the תורה set apart with a lenient sliding-scale קרבן. The גמרא tests other cases one by one: עבודה זרה, a יולדת, a מצורע and an impure נזיר. Each is rejected, either because its special rule is strict or because its קרבן is for impurity, not sin ('לכל חטאתם'). רבי שמעון learns the same limit straight from the goat's own פסוק. The גמרא then explains how each תנא reads the rest of that פסוק about the blood service in the היכל. Finally it asks why a פסוק is needed to exclude someone who knew at the beginning and at the end. It begins answering with a case where he found out just before sunset, and that answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What case of forbidden relations is left for the goat to atone for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case of גילוי עריות the goat could atone for, since both the מזיד case and the שוגג case seem to be handled some other way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Forbidden relations too, what is the case? If it was on purpose, he deserves death. If it was by accident, he must bring his own קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: Just as it did for עבודה זרה, the גמרא now asks: what case of גילוי עריות could the goat offering even be thought to atone for? Both obvious cases seem to be taken already.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sin done on purpose (מזיד) carries the death penalty, and a קרבן does not atone for that. A sin done by accident (שוגג) already has its own חטאת. So the goat seems to have no case left, and the question challenges whether the idea makes sense at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden sexual relations
What is the case? What are the exact circumstances?
On purpose, knowingly
By accident, without knowing
Someone who deserves the death penalty
Also, too

phrases.english: Forbidden relations as well, what is the case?
phrases.notes: "As well" points back to עבודה זרה, which the גמרא just asked the same question about.

phrases.english: If on purpose, he is subject to death!
If by accident, he is subject to a קרבן!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the challenge the גמרא already made about עבודה זרה, now applied to גילוי עריות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the goat might have atoned for גילוי עריות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every case already seems covered, by death if מזיד or by a personal קרבן if שוגג, so no case is left for the goat.

steps.title: On purpose without warning, or by accident without finding out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names two cases left for the goat: a מזיד sinner who was never warned, and a שוגג sinner who never found out.
steps.simpleTranslation: On purpose, but they did not warn him. By accident, but he never found out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by finding the cases that fall through the cracks of both rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without התראה (a warning from witnesses), a בית דין cannot put the sinner to death, so that sin is not covered by the death penalty. A חטאת is only brought once the sinner learns what he did, so a sinner who never found out has no קרבן yet. Those two people still need atonement, and that is where the goat could fit.

keyTerms.meaning: They warned him (gave התראה)
A warning from witnesses, which is needed before a בית דין can punish
It became known to him; he found out

phrases.english: On purpose, but they did not warn him,
phrases.notes: Without a warning from witnesses, a בית דין cannot give the death penalty.

phrases.english: by accident, but it did not become known to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to situations not covered by death or by a קרבן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every מזיד sinner gets death and every שוגג sinner brings a קרבן, so nothing is left for the goat.
steps.terutzMaskana: A מזיד sinner with no התראה, and a שוגג sinner who never found out, are both still left for the goat.

steps.title: What case of murder is left for the goat to atone for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question about שפיכות דמים. A מזיד killer gets death, and a שוגג killer goes into גלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bloodshed too, what is the case? If it was on purpose, he deserves death. If it was by accident, he must go into exile.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the same challenge to שפיכות דמים. The only change is that the accidental case is fixed by גלות, not by a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An accidental killer goes into גלות to an עיר מקלט, and that acts as his atonement. So once again both the מזיד case and the שוגג case seem to be taken, and the goat seems to have nothing left.

keyTerms.meaning: Bloodshed, murder
Exile to an עיר מקלט for someone who killed by accident
Someone who must go into exile

phrases.english: Bloodshed as well, what is the case?
If on purpose, he is subject to death!
If by accident, he is subject to exile!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 1, now applied to murder.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the goat might have atoned for שפיכות דמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מזיד killer is covered by death and a שוגג killer is covered by גלות, so no case is left for the goat.

steps.title: Same answer: no warning, or never found out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the same two cases as before: a מזיד killer who was not warned, and a שוגג killer who never found out.
steps.simpleTranslation: On purpose, but they did not warn him. By accident, but he never found out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the murder question with the very same words it used for עריות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without התראה there is no death penalty, so the deliberate killer is still left needing atonement. A killer who never learned what he did has not gone into גלות, so he is also still left needing atonement.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who killed by accident
A city of refuge where the accidental killer goes into exile
The day the goat offering brings atonement

phrases.english: On purpose, but they did not warn him,
by accident, but it did not become known to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 by repeating the answer from step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every killer is covered by death or by גלות.
steps.terutzMaskana: A killer with no התראה, or one who never found out, is still left for the goat.

steps.title: Or: accidental killers who are not sent into exile
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a second answer for murder: the goat covers accidental killings that do not carry the punishment of גלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or else, it refers to those killers who are not subject to exile.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to answer the murder question, one that only works for murder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every accidental killer goes into גלות. The תורה sends only certain kinds of accidental killers to exile. Since those other killers have no גלות to atone for them, the goat could be thought to fill that gap.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively, or else (introduces a second answer)
Those
People who are subject to exile

steps.whatToRemember: For both עריות and murder, the goat could only fit cases that slip past the normal punishment or atonement: no התראה, or never finding out. For murder there is one more case: accidental killings that do not carry גלות.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי, בְּהָנָךְ דְּלָאו בְּנֵי גָלוּת נִינְהוּ.
phrases.english: Alternatively, with those who are not subject to exile.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי, בְּהָנָךְ דְּלָאו בְּנֵי גָלוּת נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to a group of accidental killers who have no גלות
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every accidental killer goes into גלות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Some accidental killers are not sent into גלות, so the goat could cover them.

steps.title: רבי יהודה limits the goat to defiling the Temple and its sacrifices
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא. רבי יהודה learns from 'מִטֻּמְאוֹת' that the שעיר atones only for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, not for every sin called 'טומאה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: You might think the goat atones for these three 'impurities' (עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות, שפיכות דמים). So the פסוק says 'from the impurities', which means not all impurities. Which impurity do we find that the תורה set apart from all the others? Defiling the מקדש and its holy foods. So here too, the goat atones for defiling the מקדש and its holy foods. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא and quotes רבי יהודה's limit on what the שעיר atones for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה uses the word 'טומאה' for three big sins, so one might think the שעיר covers all of them. רבי יהודה reads the 'מ' in 'מִטֻּמְאוֹת' as 'some, not all.' He picks the one טומאה the תורה already treats in a special way: טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might have thought', which introduces a wrong first guess
'The verse teaches', which brings the פסוק that corrects the guess
Entering the מקדש or eating קדשים while טמא
The Torah set it apart and gave it its own special rule

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for limiting the inner שעיר of יום הכיפורים to sins of טומאה in the מקדש. The next steps test why exactly that טומאה was chosen.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: יָכוֹל עַל שָׁלֹשׁ טְומָאוֹת הַלָּלוּ
phrases.english: The Master said: One might have thought that for these three impurities
phrases.notes: These are עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות and שפיכות דמים. The Torah calls each of them 'טומאה'.

phrases.english: the goat would atone?
The verse states: "From the impurities"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:16

phrases.english: but not all impurities.
What do we find that the verse set apart
from among all the impurities?
The defiling of the Temple and its sacred foods.
So too here, for the defiling of the Temple and its sacred foods.
These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: יָכוֹל עַל שָׁלֹשׁ טְומָאוֹת הַלָּלוּ יְהֵא שָׂעִיר מְכַפֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of עריות and murder and moves on to the next line of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the inner שעיר atones only for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. It does not atone for every sin the תורה calls טומאה.

steps.title: In what way did the Torah set it apart?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יהודה means when he says the Torah 'set apart' טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'set apart' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question. This sets up the answer and the challenge that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's whole reading depends on this one טומאה being special. The גמרא wants to know exactly what makes it special.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What?' in Aramaic

phrases.english: In what way did it set it apart?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the word 'חָלַק' in רבי יהודה's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What special rule shows that the תורה set apart טומאת מקדש וקדשיו from other sins.

steps.title: It brings a sliding-scale offering
steps.stepSummary: The answer: טומאת מקדש וקדשיו is special because the sinner brings a קרבן עולה ויורד.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is set apart because one brings a sliding-scale offering for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this טומאה is special because of the type of קרבן it requires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most sins done by mistake require a fixed חטאת. For טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, the קרבן depends on how much the sinner can afford. That unusual rule is what makes it 'set apart'.

keyTerms.meaning: A sliding-scale offering: an animal, birds or flour, depending on what the person can afford
'That he brings'

phrases.english: That one brings a sliding-scale offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תורה set apart טומאת מקדש וקדשיו by requiring a קרבן עולה ויורד.

steps.title: Idol worship is also set apart, so why not that?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: עבודה זרה also has a special rule, a female goat and not a female lamb. So maybe the שעיר atones for עבודה זרה instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then say the goat atones for idol worship! How is it set apart? (A memory aid: idol worship, a woman after childbirth, a leper, a nazir, and so on.) One brings a female goat and not a female lamb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 8. If 'having a special קרבן' is enough, then עבודה זרה fits too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For most mistaken sins, a person may bring a female lamb or a female goat. For עבודה זרה, only a female goat is allowed, so it is also 'set apart'. That makes it unclear why רבי יהודה chose טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. The memory-aid line lists the other cases the גמרא will raise next in the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say instead', used to suggest a different option
A memory aid listing the cases that are coming up
A female goat
A female lamb

steps.confusionAlert: The line in round brackets is not part of the argument. It is only a memory aid that lists the next cases the גמרא will raise. The sentence continues right after it with 'דְּמַיְיתֵי שְׂעִירָה'.

phrases.english: Say instead idol worship,
and in what way is it set apart?

phrases.aramaic: (סִימַן: עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, יוֹלֶדֶת, מְצוֹרָע, נָזִיר וְכוּ׳)
phrases.english: (Mnemonic: idol worship, a woman after childbirth, a leper, a nazirite, etc.)
That one brings a female goat and not a female lamb!
phrases.notes: For other sins a female lamb also works. For עבודה זרה only a female goat is allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 8 by showing another sin that is also 'set apart'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the קרבן עולה ויורד is what makes טומאת מקדש וקדשיו the one the Torah set apart.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If any special קרבן rule counts as 'set apart', then עבודה זרה, which requires only a female goat, should qualify just as well. That leaves רבי יהודה's choice unexplained.

steps.title: Set apart to be lenient, not to be strict
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that רבי יהודה meant a sin set apart for leniency. עבודה זרה is set apart for strictness, so it does not fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: We are talking about something the Torah set apart to make it easier. This case (עבודה זרה) was set apart to make it harder.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers the challenge from step 9. He explains that עבודה זרה does not fit the kind of 'special rule' רבי יהודה had in mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both טומאת מקדש וקדשיו and עבודה זרה have special rules for their קרבן. With טומאת מקדש וקדשיו the special rule is a lighter one: a poor person can bring a cheaper קרבן עולה ויורד. With עבודה זרה the special rule makes it harder, so it is a different kind of 'set apart' and the שעיר does not go to it.

keyTerms.meaning: set apart, gave a special rule
to be lenient, to make easier
to be strict, to make harder
we were saying, what we meant was

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives us the test for the rest of the סוגיא: the case we want is one the תורה set apart to be lenient.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
We were speaking of a case set apart to be lenient,
phrases.notes: He means the special cheaper קרבן עולה ויורד, which makes things easier for the sinner.

phrases.english: but this one is set apart to be strict.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 about עבודה זרה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the earlier statement more narrowly (set apart to be lenient only)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any sin with a special קרבן rule, even a stricter one like עבודה זרה, might be what the שעיר atones for.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a sin set apart to be lenient counts, so עבודה זרה is out.

steps.title: Maybe the goat atones for a woman after childbirth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a יולדת, who also brings a lenient קרבן עולה ויורד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then say it means a woman after childbirth. She was set apart too, because she brings a sliding-scale offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses רב כהנא's new test and finds another case that seems to pass it: a יולדת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יולדת also brings a קרבן עולה ויורד, which is a leniency. So by the rule 'set apart to be lenient', she seems just as good a match as טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.

keyTerms.meaning: a woman who has just given birth
say instead, maybe it means
sliding-scale offering, depends on how much money the person has

phrases.english: Say instead a woman after childbirth, who was set apart,
since she brings a sliding-scale offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the 'set apart to be lenient' test from step 10 to suggest a new case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the שעיר atones for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A יולדת also has a lenient special rule, so she meets the same test.

steps.title: The goat covers sins, not impurities
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא answers from the פסוק 'לכל חטאתם': the שעיר atones for sins, and a יולדת brings her קרבן for impurity, not for a sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא said: The פסוק says 'for all their sins,' not 'for all their impurities.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הושעיא rejects the יולדת by pointing to the exact words of the פסוק about the שעיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the goat atones 'לכל חטאתם', for sins. A יולדת did not sin. Her קרבן comes because she was impure. So the שעיר is not for her.

keyTerms.meaning: for all their sins
their impurities

steps.confusionAlert: A יולדת brings a קרבן חטאת, but here the גמרא treats it as coming because of her impurity, not because she did something wrong.

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya said:
"For all their sins"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:16

phrases.english: and not "for all their impurities."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the יולדת challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the exact wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any lenient special case, including a יולדת, could be what the goat atones for.
steps.terutzMaskana: The goat atones only for sins. A יולדת's קרבן is for impurity, so she is not included.

steps.title: What about the view that a יולדת is a sinner?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: according to רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, a יולדת is a sinner, so רב הושעיא's answer does not work for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, who says a woman after childbirth is also a sinner, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הושעיא's answer from a תנא who holds that a יולדת's קרבן is for a sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הושעיא's answer depends on the idea that a יולדת did not sin. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי holds that she did sin, so for him she would fit 'לכל חטאתם'. Then why wouldn't the goat atone for her?

keyTerms.meaning: a woman who sinned
also
what is there to say? (how do we answer?)

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai,
who says a woman after childbirth is also a sinner,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי דְּאָמַר יוֹלֶדֶת נָמֵי חוֹטֵאת הִיא מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 12 by bringing in another תנא's view.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי שמעון בן יוחאי a יולדת is a sinner, so 'לכל חטאתם' could include her.

steps.title: רבי שמעון learns it from the goat's own פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון does not need the 'set apart' argument at all. He learns straight from the goat's own פסוק what it atones for.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון follows his own reasoning, as he said: the matter is decided from its own place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון has a different source, so the יולדת question does not bother him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'set apart to be lenient' argument belongs to רבי יהודה. רבי שמעון said in the ברייתא that the goat's own פסוק already tells us it is for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. So for him there is no opening to suggest a יולדת.

keyTerms.meaning: following his own reasoning
it is decided from its own place (its own פסוק)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon follows his own reasoning,
as he said: it is decided from its own place.
phrases.notes: This is his line from the ברייתא. The goat's own פסוק already tells us what it is for, so he doesn't need רבי יהודה's argument.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְטַעְמֵיהּ דְּאָמַר מִמְּקוֹמוֹ הוּא מוּכְרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a different source used by רבי שמעון
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון, like רבי יהודה, relies on 'set apart', so a יולדת who sinned might be included.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון learns directly from the goat's פסוק, so the יולדת question does not arise for him.

steps.title: Maybe the goat atones for a מצורע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a מצורע, who also brings a lenient קרבן עולה ויורד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then say it means a מצורע!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי יהודה's 'set apart to be lenient' test and suggests one more case that seems to pass it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A poor מצורע brings a cheaper קרבן, which is also a leniency. So he seems to fit the test just like טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.

keyTerms.meaning: a person with צרעת, a skin disease that makes one impure

phrases.english: Say instead a person with צרעת!
phrases.notes: The reason is left unsaid, as with the יולדת: he also brings a cheaper offering if he is poor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side question about רבי שמעון, returns to testing new cases under רבי יהודה's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the שעיר atones for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מצורע also has a lenient special rule for his קרבן, so he meets the same test.

steps.title: Same answer: sins, not impurities
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא gives the same answer. A מצורע's קרבן is for impurity, and the goat covers only sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא said: The פסוק says 'for all their sins,' not 'for all their impurities.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the מצורע with the exact same answer it used for the יולדת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מצורע's קרבן comes to purify him from his impurity. It is not for a sin. Since the goat atones only 'לכל חטאתם', the מצורע is excluded, and טומאת מקדש וקדשיו stays as the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: a sin, something done wrong
ritual impurity

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, the inner שעיר atones only for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. עבודה זרה is out because its special rule is strict. יולדת and מצורע are out because their קרבנות are for impurity, not sin ('לכל חטאתם'). רבי שמעון learns it straight from the goat's own פסוק.

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya said:
"For all their sins"
and not "for all their impurities."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מצורע challenge of step 15 using the same source as step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the exact wording of the פסוק (repeated)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A מצורע, who has a lenient special קרבן, could be what the goat atones for.
steps.terutzMaskana: A מצורע's קרבן is for impurity, not sin, so the goat does not atone for him.

steps.title: What about the view that a מצורע is a sinner?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב הושעיא's answer can work for רבי שמואל בר נחמני, who holds that נגעים come because of sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי שמואל בר נחמני, who says that leprous marks come because of seven kinds of sins, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 16. If a מצורע is really a sinner, then saying his קרבן is only for impurity does not seem to work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 said the goat cannot cover a מצורע because his קרבן is for impurity, not for a sin. רבי שמואל בר נחמני holds that נגעים are a punishment for sin. So for him a מצורע is a sinner, and the goat might cover him after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Leprous marks (צרעת)
Seven matters, meaning seven kinds of sins
What is there to say? (a formula that opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: עַל שִׁבְעָה דְּבָרִים נְגָעִים בָּאִין –
phrases.english: who says: leprous marks come because of seven things,
phrases.notes: He means seven kinds of sins. So for him, a מצורע is someone who sinned.

phrases.english: what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי, דְּאָמַר: עַל שִׁבְעָה דְּבָרִים נְגָעִים בָּאִין – מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 16 by using a view that treats a מצורע as a sinner.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הושעיא's claim that a מצורע's קרבן is for impurity and not for sin
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If נגעים come because of sins, then the מצורע is a sinner. In that case the goat, which covers sins, could cover him too.

steps.title: The נגע atones for the sin, and the קרבן lets him back into the community
steps.stepSummary: The נגע itself atones for the sin. The קרבן is only to let the מצורע rejoin the community.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is his leprous mark that atones for him. The קרבן is brought so that he is allowed back into the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that even if a מצורע did sin, his suffering from the נגע already atoned for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא splits the two jobs. The נגע handles the sin. The קרבן only lets him return to the community. So the קרבן still is not a sin-offering, and the goat is not needed to cover it.

keyTerms.meaning: His נגע is what atones for him
To be allowed back into the community

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a קרבן can have a purpose other than atonement. Here its purpose is to let the person rejoin the community.

phrases.english: There, it is his mark that atones for him,
and the offering is to permit him to rejoin the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the purpose of the קרבן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a מצורע sinned, his קרבן would be for sin, and the goat would cover him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The נגע already atoned for the sin. The קרבן only lets him rejoin the community, so the goat is still not involved.

steps.title: Maybe the goat atones for an impure נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the impure נזיר, who is set apart because he brings birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say the goat atones for an impure נזיר, who is set apart because he brings turtledoves or young pigeons!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another person who brings an unusual, lighter קרבן and might be the one the goat covers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the יולדת and the מצורע before, the impure נזיר is 'set apart' with a קרבן of birds. So he might fit the pattern of the person whose sin the goat covers.

keyTerms.meaning: A נזיר who became impure
Set apart, treated differently
Turtledoves or young pigeons

phrases.english: But say an impure nazirite,
who is set apart, since he brings turtledoves or young pigeons!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new candidate after the מצורע was rejected.
steps.kashyaTarget: The search for which 'set apart' person the goat covers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The impure נזיר also brings a special bird קרבן, so he might be the one meant.

steps.title: Sins, not impurities
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא answers again: the goat covers sins, not impurities.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא said: The פסוק says 'for all their sins,' not 'for all their impurities.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הושעיא uses the same answer as before. The impure נזיר's קרבן is for impurity, so the goat does not cover it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'לכל חטאתם' limit the goat to sins. A נזיר who became impure is bringing a קרבן because of impurity, not because of a sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Their impurities

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya said:
"For all their sins" – and not for all their impurities.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:16

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא: לְכׇל חַטֹּאתָם – וְלֹא לְכׇל טוּמְאֹתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19 with the same rule used in Steps 12 and 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The goat might cover the impure נזיר, who is set apart.
steps.terutzMaskana: The goat covers only sins, and the נזיר's קרבן is for impurity.

steps.title: What about the view that a נזיר is a sinner?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר הקפר holds that a נזיר is a sinner, so רב הושעיא's answer does not seem to work for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי אלעזר הקפר, who says a נזיר is also a sinner, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 20 using רבי אלעזר הקפר's view. It is the same kind of challenge as Steps 13 and 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a נזיר counts as a sinner, then his קרבן could be connected to sin. Then 'sins, not impurities' would not rule him out.

keyTerms.meaning: Sinner

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Elazar HaKappar,
who says a nazirite is also a sinner,
phrases.notes: He means the נזיר held himself back from wine when he didn't have to.

phrases.english: what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הַקַּפָּר, דְּאָמַר נָזִיר נָמֵי חוֹטֵא הוּא, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the נזיר's קרבן is not for a sin
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי אלעזר הקפר a נזיר is a sinner, so the goat could cover him.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר הקפר holds like רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר הקפר holds like רבי שמעון, who learns straight from the goat's own פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי שמעון, who says: it is decided from its own place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר הקפר does not use the 'set apart' approach at all. He follows רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון learns what the goat atones for from the goat's own פסוק, not from comparing it to people who are 'set apart.' So the question about the נזיר never comes up for him. This is the same kind of answer as Step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: It is decided from its own place, meaning from the goat's own פסוק
He holds like

steps.whatToRemember: When a view calls the 'set apart' person a sinner, the גמרא answers in one of two ways. For רבי שמעון בן יוחאי (יולדת) and רבי אלעזר הקפר (נזיר), that view learns from the goat's own פסוק instead. For רבי שמואל בר נחמני (מצורע), the נגע itself atones and the קרבן only lets him rejoin the community.

phrases.english: He holds like Rabbi Shimon,
who says: it is decided from its own place.
phrases.notes: This is the same idea we saw in Step 14.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, דְּאָמַר: מִמְּקוֹמוֹ הוּא מוּכְרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the view to a different method of learning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר הקפר would have to say the goat covers the נזיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: He follows רבי שמעון and learns from the goat's own פסוק, so the 'set apart' argument does not apply to him.

steps.title: Going back to רבי שמעון's words in the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון from the ברייתא: the goat atones for making holy things impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: רבי שמעון says: it is decided from its own place. The פסוק says 'And he shall atone for the holy place from the impurities,' meaning for the impurity of holy things, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back רבי שמעון's words from the ברייתא so it can look at them more closely. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון reads the goat's own פסוק to say that it atones for impurity that touched holy things, like the מקדש or its קדשים. Here the ברייתא is quoted again for a new purpose: to compare רבי שמעון with רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall atone for the holy place from the impurities
Impurity that touches holy things

phrases.english: The Master said: Rabbi Shimon says:
it is decided from its own place;
as it says:
"And he shall atone for the holy place from the impurities" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:16

phrases.english: for the impurity of holy things, etc.
phrases.notes: כו׳ means 'and so on.' The rest of רבי שמעון's words in the ברייתא are left out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: מִמְּקוֹמוֹ הוּא מוּכְרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא that Step 22 mentioned, now to analyze it in its own right.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון learns from the goat's own פסוק that it atones for impurity of holy things.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's reading sounds right, so why does רבי יהודה disagree?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי שמעון's reading makes good sense and asks why רבי יהודה does not accept it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון is saying something good!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא praises רבי שמעון's reading. Doing that really asks why רבי יהודה needed a different way to learn the law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the goat's own פסוק clearly says what it atones for, then רבי יהודה's longer method looks unnecessary. The challenge is aimed at רבי יהודה, not at רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: He is saying well, meaning his point is convincing

steps.confusionAlert: This line praises רבי שמעון, but it is really a challenge to רבי יהודה. The question is why he doesn't learn the same way.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon is saying well!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי שמעון's reading to question רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's choice not to learn from the goat's own פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק seems to state plainly what the goat atones for. So why would רבי יהודה learn it another way?

steps.title: רבי יהודה needs that פסוק for how the blood is sprinkled
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה uses the פסוק to teach that the blood service in the היכל is done the same way as in the קודש הקדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה would tell you: that פסוק is needed to teach that just as he does the service inside the קודש הקדשים, so he should do it in the היכל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יהודה. He uses the פסוק to teach something else, so he cannot use it to learn what the goat atones for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, 'וכפר על הקדש' teaches about the order of the blood service. The sprinkling done in the inner room is repeated the same way in the היכל. Since the פסוק is used for that, he learns the goat's atonement from a different source.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it for something else
The innermost room, the קודש הקדשים
The Sanctuary room outside the קודש הקדשים

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון learns what the goat atones for from its own פסוק. רבי יהודה uses that same פסוק to teach that the blood service in the היכל matches the service in the קודש הקדשים.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda would say to you:
that verse is needed for him
to teach that just as he performs it in the innermost chamber,
so he shall perform it in the Sanctuary.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אָמַר לָךְ: הַהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The פסוק is needed to teach something else
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה should learn what the goat atones for from its own פסוק, as רבי שמעון does.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה needs that פסוק to teach that the service in the היכל is done like the service in the קודש הקדשים.

steps.title: Where רבי שמעון learns the היכל service
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי שמעון uses the first phrase for טומאה, he learns the היכל blood service from 'וכן יעשה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון? He learns that rule from 'And so shall he do'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי שמעון gets the rule that רבי יהודה learned in Step 25, and it answers right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 25, רבי יהודה used the phrase about atoning for the קודש to teach that the היכל service matches the inner service. רבי שמעון already used that phrase for טומאה, so he needs another source. He finds it in the next words of the same פסוק, 'וכן יעשה לאהל מועד'.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And so shall he do', which tells us to repeat the same service
It is derived from
The Tent of Meeting; here it means the היכל

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon, where does he learn it?
phrases.notes: The question is left unspoken. Since he used the first phrase for טומאה, where does he get the היכל rule?

phrases.english: That is derived from 'And so shall he do'.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:16

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן – הַהוּא מִ״וְּכֵן יַעֲשֶׂה״ נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies רבי שמעון's source for the rule that רבי יהודה derived in Step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternate source within the same פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון learns that the היכל service matches the inner service from 'וכן יעשה לאהל מועד'.

steps.title: Why רבי יהודה needs both phrases
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יהודה had only 'וכן יעשה', he might think a new bull and goat are needed for the היכל. The extra phrase teaches that the same ones are used.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? If we had only that phrase, I would have said to bring another bull and goat and do the service with them. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יהודה is not satisfied with 'וכן יעשה' alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'וכן יעשה' could mean 'do the same kind of service again', even with new animals. רבי יהודה's extra phrase teaches that the blood of the very same bull and goat is used in the היכל.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)
The bull and goat of יום כיפור
Other, different ones
It teaches us

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda, why does he need the other phrase?
If it were only from that phrase, I would have said
phrases.notes: 'That phrase' means 'וכן יעשה'.

phrases.english: let him bring another bull and goat and perform the service with them;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the obvious follow-up: if 'וכן יעשה' exists, why does רבי יהודה need the earlier phrase?
steps.terutzHavaAmina: New animals would be brought for the היכל service.
steps.terutzMaskana: The same bull and goat are used for the היכל service.

steps.title: רבי שמעון reads 'same animals' from 'וכן יעשה' itself
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says the words 'וכן יעשה' already show that the same bull and goat are used.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון? 'And so shall he do to the Tent of Meeting' already shows it on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי שמעון does not worry about the mistake described in Step 27.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, 'וכן', meaning 'and in this same way', already points to continuing with the same blood. So he needs no extra phrase, and the first phrase stays free for his טומאה teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: It is understood from the phrase itself

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים agree on the הלכה that the same bull and goat are used in the היכל. They only disagree about which words of ויקרא 16:16 teach it.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon says:
'And so shall he do to the Tent of Meeting'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:16

phrases.english: is understood from itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, ״וְכֵן יַעֲשֶׂה לְאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד״ – מִינֵּיהּ מַשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי שמעון's reply to רבי יהודה's reason in Step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the single phrase as covering both points
steps.terutzMaskana: 'וכן יעשה' teaches both that the היכל service matches and that the same animals are used.

steps.title: The ברייתא limits what the goat atones for
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the goat does not atone for every kind of טומאה in the מקדש, based on 'מפשעיהם לכל חטאתם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: You might think this goat atones for every case of טומאה in the מקדש. So the פסוק says: 'from their rebellions, for all their sins'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא and quotes its next line, so that it can analyze it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns from the פסוק that the goat's atonement has limits, so some טומאה cases are not included. The next step asks exactly which case is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought
The פסוק teaches
Atones

phrases.english: The Master said:
One might have thought that for all impurities of the Temple
this goat would atone?
The verse states:
'From their rebellions, for all their sins, etc.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:16

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא after finishing the side discussion between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The inner goat does not atone for every case of טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.

steps.title: Which case is left out?
steps.stepSummary: The case the goat does not cover is one where the person knew at the beginning and also knew at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which case is it? One where there was awareness at the beginning and awareness at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which case the ברייתא excluded and names it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who knew he was טמא, forgot, and later remembered is the person who brings a קרבן עולה ויורד. The גמרא identifies him as the case the goat does not cover, and this sets up the challenge that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Awareness at the beginning, before the sin
Awareness at the end, after the sin

phrases.english: What is it?
Where there is awareness at the beginning
and there is awareness at the end;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the case that Step 29 excluded.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which טומאה case the goat does not atone for
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Awareness both at the beginning and at the end

steps.title: He brings his own קרבן anyway
steps.stepSummary: That person is already obligated in a קרבן, so the פסוק seems unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this person is someone who brings a קרבן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need for the פסוק to exclude this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone with awareness at the beginning and at the end brings his own קרבן עולה ויורד. It seems obvious that the goat would not replace his personal obligation, so why would the ברייתא need a פסוק for it?

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who is obligated to bring a קרבן

phrases.english: But this one is subject to an offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the need for the derivation, based on the case defined in Step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's need for 'מפשעיהם לכל חטאתם'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person who is obligated in his own קרבן would obviously not be covered by the communal goat, so the פסוק would be teaching nothing new.

steps.title: Finding out just before sunset
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק is needed for someone who found out close to sunset before יום כיפור and could not bring his קרבן in time.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where he found out close to sunset. You might have thought that until he brings his קרבן...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק covers a special timing case, and it begins to explain the mistaken idea the פסוק comes to prevent. The explanation continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he found out right before יום כיפור, he had no chance to bring his קרבן beforehand. We might think the goat at least protects him in the meantime, until he can bring it. The פסוק teaches that the goat does not cover him even then.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for a special case

steps.confusionAlert: The person still brings his own קרבן after יום כיפור. The question is only whether the goat covers him during the time before he brings it.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
where he became aware close to sunset.
phrases.notes: He means sunset right before יום כיפור begins, so there is no time left to bring his קרבן.

steps.terutzMaskana: Even in this case, the goat does not atone for him.
